chains.title: Ref G allele strengthens a TCF/LEF site bound by TCF7L2 in the 8q24 enhancer, raising MYC/CCAT2 output in colonic epithelium
chains.cell_type: colonic epithelial / colorectal cancer cells (HCT 116, ACH-000971)

links.claim: A qbic_tf_detail lookup of TCF7L2 shows it is covered only through CIS-BP-mapped models of related HMG/Sox factors (LEF1, TCF7, TCF7L1), i.e. coverage 'mapped'. Two of these models pass the gate with negative effects (LEF1 effect -0.47, z -4.66; TCF7 effect -0.229, z -4.59), so the reference G allele is predicted to bind the TCF/LEF specificity more strongly; the effects are modest and rank only ~350/997, so this is weak binding evidence on its own. ENCODE ChIP-seq shows one TCF7L2 peak in HCT116 containing the variant (and three in HepG2), so the factor does occupy this site in the relevant line.

The variant lies in pELS cCRE EH38E3858447 with high DNase (z 5.2) and H3K27ac (z 4.8) and in Ensembl enhancer ENSR8_CGMBX; the z-scores are maxima over biosamples, but TCF7L2 occupancy in HCT116 shows the site is bound in a colon line.

The element sits in the 8q24 gene desert; MYC is the nearest classical oncogene at 334 kb and a colon goblet-cell sceQTL for PVT1 (PIP 0.95) is in the same credible set, consistent with action on the MYC/PVT1 region. This is distance- and QTL-adjacent support only: L2G scores MYC 0.05 against POU5F1B 0.89, and no cited eQTL or CRISPR links this element to MYC.
HCT116 is a Wnt-pathway-active colorectal line in which TCF7L2 binds this exact position (ENCSR000EUV); no cited evidence demonstrates colon-specific enhancer activity beyond that.

Most colorectal rows in the GWAS Catalog list G as the effect allele (colorectal cancer or advanced adenoma p 3e-64, benign neoplasm of colon, colon polyps, colon cancer), matching a G-preferring TCF7L2 site; the top row lists T, so the sign convention is not internally consistent and the direction remains unresolved by cited evidence.

chains.title: Alt T allele creates a T-box site that raises POU5F1B, the eQTL- and L2G-nominated effector gene

links.claim: QBiC-SELEX group G101 (T-box) shows a large alt gain (TBX19 own model, z 26.18, effect +4.18; site strength ref 79.0th to alt 99.9th percentile). Within the group TBXT is 0 TPM and TBX19 1.92 TPM in this line, so TBX19 is named by expression alone; the choice is weak and no ChIP or EMSA evidence supports T-box occupancy here.
The site is an active pELS enhancer (DNase z 5.2, H3K27ac z 4.8) in which a de novo high-affinity T-box site could raise activity.

GTEx v8 shows a significant colon-transverse eQTL in which the alt T allele raises POU5F1B (NES +0.20, p 8.2e-06), the same direction as the predicted alt binding gain; Open Targets L2G nominates POU5F1B (0.82-0.89) and the variant lies in the POU5F1B gene body.
The effect gene is measured in transverse colon, the disease-relevant tissue, and TBX19 is expressed (1.92 TPM) in the HCT 116 context; expression only, no occupancy shown.

POU5F1B fosters proliferation and metastatic potential of CRC cells, so higher POU5F1B on the T allele could raise risk; however most colorectal GWAS rows name G as the effect allele, which conflicts with this direction.

TBX19 depletion removes the allelic reporter difference

Element perturbation changes MYC/CCAT2 but not POU5F1B

chains.title: Ref G allele is bound by the BTB-ZF factor ZBTB43, whose loss on the T allele de-represses the enhancer

links.claim: QBiC-SELEX group G404 contains only ZBTB43 (own model), z -23.26, effect -1.724: the reference G allele binds more strongly (ref 99.8th vs alt 87.9th percentile). No within-group choice is needed, but this is a binding prediction alone with no ChIP or EMSA support, and the repressor role of ZBTB43 is an assumption.
The variant sits in an active pELS enhancer; loss of a repressive BTB-ZF site there would raise its activity.
Higher activity on the T allele matches the only cited colon eQTL, POU5F1B up on T (NES +0.20), and POU5F1B is the L2G-nominated gene; the connection of ZBTB43 to that gene is not shown.
ZBTB43 is expressed at 8.32 TPM in the HCT 116 context; expression only, no occupancy shown.
Increased 8q24 enhancer output in colonic epithelium is consistent with the strong colorectal associations at rs6983267, though the risk-allele direction across GWAS rows is inconsistent.

predictions: ZBTB43 CUT&RUN shows G-biased occupancy at the cCRE
ZBTB43 knockdown raises reporter activity only for the G allele
The allelic difference is independent of TCF/LEF and of Wnt inhibition
falsified_if: ZBTB43 does not occupy the locus in colon cells
ZBTB43 depletion has no effect on reporter activity or on POU5F1B/MYC

chains.title: Alt T allele strengthens a nuclear-receptor half-site read by HNF4A, altering enhancer output on CCAT2/POU5F1B

links.claim: QBiC-SELEX group G372 (nuclear receptor specificity) shows a very strong alt-preferring change (best model NR2E1, z 53.69, effect +1.968; ref 96.7th to alt 99.6th percentile). The group names a shared specificity: its only passing member NR2E1 is 0 TPM, while the group row lists HNF4A (own model, 2.95 TPM) and HNF4G (own model, 2.24 TPM) as expressed, and HNF4A is the dominant intestinal nuclear receptor, so HNF4A is chosen by expression plus tissue identity. No model of HNF4A itself is reported as passing, so its direction is inferred from the shared specificity and is weak. A broader nuclear-receptor group (G002) also shows alt gain but with members disagreeing on direction.
The variant lies in an active pELS enhancer (DNase z 5.2, H3K27ac z 4.8), where a gained nuclear-receptor site could change output.
The variant is exonic in CCAT2 and the cCRE's nearby genes are CCAT2/PCAT1/POU5F1B; the only cited allele-dependent expression in colon is POU5F1B (alt-raising), so CCAT2 rests on proximity alone.
HNF4A is expressed in this colorectal line (2.95 TPM) whereas NR2E1 is not; expression only, no occupancy shown.
CCAT2 is repeatedly implicated in gastrointestinal cancer progression, so a change in CCAT2 level could alter CRC risk; no cited quote ties CCAT2 level to this allele.

HNF4A knockdown removes the allelic reporter difference
The allelic difference survives Wnt/TCF inhibition
CCAT2, not MYC or POU5F1B, responds to element perturbation

grades_v0.reason: No cited evidence (E01, E04) shows TCF7L2 binding or any allele preference. The claim admits the direction comes from memory of the literature, and TCF7L2 coverage was never checked. It is also inconsistent with the G-binds-more and risk-allele framing, since E04 lists T as the colorectal effect allele in the top association.

E03 places the variant in pELS EH38E3858447 with DNase z 5.2 and H3K27ac z 4.8, and E01 gives the enhancer feature ENSR8_CGMBX. These are maxima over biosamples, so activity in colon is not shown, but the element link holds.

MYC is 334 kb away (E02), and E05 gives it L2G 0.05 against POU5F1B 0.89. The only MYC-adjacent evidence is a PVT1 sceQTL with PIP 0.95 in colon goblet cells. No cited evidence shows CRISPR or an eQTL for MYC, and the claim that CCAT2 and PCAT1 act in cis on MYC is uncited. The claim also wrongly calls MYC the nearest protein-coding gene, since POU5F1B is nearer.
E03 gives only biosample-maximum z-scores, with no HCT 116 or colon-specific data. The claim that Wnt is constitutively on is not supported by the cited evidence.

The strong colorectal association in E04 and E06a is genetic, but it does not connect to MYC dosage or proliferation through any cited mechanism. The allele direction is unresolved: the top GWAS effect allele is T, while several other colon traits list G.

The QBiC-SELEX group G372 signal is strong (z 53.69, alt binds more), but its best model is NR2E1, which is 0 TPM. HNF4A was picked from the group by expression and by prior knowledge of the intestine, and HNF4A is not named as a passing member. The own-model coverage claim is not shown by any row or lookup of HNF4A, so qbic_tf_detail should be run. The binding prediction alone is at most weak.
E03 shows active pELS marks (DNase z 5.2, H3K27ac z 4.8). This establishes the element but not a role for HNF4A.

The variant lies in a CCAT2 exon (E01), and CCAT2 is listed as a nearby gene of the cCRE (E03). Proximity is the only support, and no QTL, CRISPR or L2G evidence ties the enhancer to CCAT2 regulation.
E08 gives HNF4A 2.95 TPM in the HCT 116 context, which shows expression only. It does not show HNF4A occupancy or function at this site.
E06 gives general literature on CCAT2 in gastrointestinal cancer, but no quote links CCAT2 level to risk at this variant. The risk direction is not established.

The QBiC-SELEX result for ZBTB43 is a strong ref-preferring change (z -23.26, own model, consistent with E12). It is a binding prediction alone. ZBTB43 as a repressor is an assumption, and no ChIP evidence is cited.
E03 shows the element is active, but nothing shows a repressive BTB-ZF site acting in it. The repressor mechanism is assumed.
MYC is chosen at 334 kb (E02) with no E03 link to MYC, and E05 gives it L2G 0.05. POU5F1B has far stronger genetic support than MYC. No perturbation or eQTL is cited for MYC.
E12 gives 8.32 TPM for ZBTB43, which shows expression in the context only. It is not the highest of all TFs, since MBNL2 has 26 TPM and the nuclear receptor group has many higher.

E04 shows the colorectal association, but the direction does not fit: a G allele that binds a repressor would lower enhancer activity, while the claim ties higher MYC to risk without evidence of the allele's direction.

The QBiC-SELEX prediction for the T-box group is strong (z 26.18, alt gain). TBX19 was chosen only by expression at 1.92 TPM, which the claim itself calls weak. Expression is low, and TBXT is 0 TPM. No ChIP or EMSA evidence is cited.
E03 shows an active pELS, but nothing shows a T-box factor regulates it.

E05 gives POU5F1B an L2G of 0.82-0.89 in credible sets with PIP 1.00, and E06b shows the TWAS prioritises POU5F1B. This is genetic support for the gene, not perturbation. E02 shows the variant is in the POU5F1B gene body and E01 gives an intron variant. It supports POU5F1B as the effector gene but not the specific enhancer-promoter link.
E11 gives TBX19 at 1.92 TPM in HCT 116, an expression filter only. No cell-type-specific enhancer activity or POU5F1B expression is shown.

E06c quotes that POU5F1B fosters CRC cell proliferation and metastatic potential, which is a functional perturbation result in the cancer phenotype. The link from the variant to increased POU5F1B is not itself shown, and the quote comes from E06c while E06b is TWAS, so the sign for this allele remains unestablished.

grades_final.reason: TCF7L2 is only 'mapped' via LEF1/TCF7 models. The ref-preferring effects are modest (-0.47, -0.229) and the TCF7 site strength rises on alt (96.9 to 99.2), which contradicts the direction. A HCT116 ChIP peak (E19) shows occupancy but not allelic preference. Nothing cited shows an allelic difference.
E01 and E03 place the variant in a pELS cCRE with high DNase and H3K27ac and in an Ensembl enhancer. The z-scores are maxima over biosamples, but the TCF7L2 peak in HCT116 adds colon-line context.

MYC rests on distance (334 kb) and a PVT1 sceQTL in the same credible set. L2G gives MYC 0.05 against POU5F1B 0.89, and no eQTL or CRISPR evidence links the element to MYC. The only colon eQTL in E20 is for POU5F1B.
A TCF7L2 peak in HCT116 is occupancy context only. It does not show colon-specific enhancer activity or an allele effect. The Wnt-active description of HCT116 is not in the cited evidence.

GWAS rows are mixed on effect allele (the top colorectal row lists T, others G), so direction is unresolved. E06a only reports the locus association and does not tie a G-preferring TCF7L2 site to MYC or risk.

A strong alt gain in the T-box group (z 26.18) is a prediction alone. TBX19 was chosen by expression alone (TBXT is 0 TPM), with no ChIP or EMSA support. The model direction (alt binds more) matches the claim.
The pELS enhancer marks (E03) are maxima over biosamples. The claim that a de novo T-box site raises activity is an inference with no perturbation or reporter evidence.

The GTEx colon-transverse eQTL (E20) shows POU5F1B up on alt (NES +0.20), and the Open Targets L2G for POU5F1B is 0.82-0.89. The TWAS (E06b) names POU5F1B. This is genetic support for the variant-gene link, though it does not show that the T-box factor mediates it.
Transverse colon is the tissue of the eQTL, but TBX19 expression at 1.92 TPM in HCT116 is context only and shows no occupancy. The eQTL is not from HCT116.

E06c shows POU5F1B promotes CRC cell proliferation and metastasis, which fits higher POU5F1B raising risk. The GWAS effect-allele direction is mostly G and conflicts with this chain, so the link is only partly consistent.

HNF4A is inferred from a group whose only passing member is NR2E1 (0 TPM). No HNF4A model is shown to pass the gate. HNF4A was chosen by expression and tissue identity, and no qbic_tf_detail lookup of HNF4A is cited. The G002 group disagrees on direction. The claim cites NR2E1's binding change for a different TF.
The enhancer marks (E03) are maxima over biosamples. The claim that a gained nuclear-receptor site alters output is speculative, with no perturbation or reporter evidence.
The variant is exonic in CCAT2 and the cCRE lists CCAT2 as a nearby gene, so the link rests on proximity alone. The only allele-dependent colon expression cited is for POU5F1B, not CCAT2.
HNF4A is expressed at 2.95 TPM, but this is expression only. No ChIP or occupancy of HNF4A at the site is shown.
E06 gives only review-level titles linking CCAT2 to GI cancer. No quote ties CCAT2 level to this allele or to CRC risk, so this is an over-reach.
The ZBTB43 own-model prediction (z -23.26, ref binds more) is consistent with the claim. It is a binding prediction alone with no ChIP or EMSA support, and the repressor role is an assumption.
The cCRE is active (E03), but the claim that a repressive BTB-ZF site there would raise activity is an unsupported assumption.
The POU5F1B eQTL and L2G (E20, E05) support the variant-gene link in general. Nothing connects ZBTB43 to POU5F1B, as the claim itself concedes.
ZBTB43 at 8.32 TPM is expression only, with no occupancy. The ZBTB43 expression value is cited from E12.
The strong colorectal associations (E04) are general. The effect-allele direction is inconsistent across rows, and no evidence ties ZBTB43 or enhancer output to risk.
